LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To give and follow simple directions and instructions.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To talk about things you can see in different places 
in the world and things you can buy or do in a shop.

2.– STUDENT STORYTELLING WITH CHANGES (14’)
Today the students can tell the whole story choosing new 
variables. You can also encourage them to get up and act out 
the story, pretending to be the different characters and moving 
around the classroom as if it were a stage.
NOTE: if your group still struggles with telling the story or 
you are short on time, have them tell it without any changes.
3.– ACTIVITY 7: DIRECTIONS SONG (TR#13) (3’)
> Main Activity
To perform the song, have the Ss stand with their back against 
the wall in a line, side by side. Then the first time they sing the 
song they will simply turn left and right while standing in place 
and then walk straight ahead when the song says to do so. 
The second time you do the activity, they must line up behind 
one another forming a train, holding onto the shoulders of the 
S in front of them. Then, this time, when the song says turn left 
and right, they will actually walk around the room while doing 
so. The song will speed up so make sure the Ss are ready to 
do the actions quickly. 
DIRECTIONS SONG
Turn left, left, left
Turn right, right, right
Walk straight ahead
Straight, straight, straight
That was great! Now line up! Ready? Steady? Go! 
Turn left, left, left
Turn right, right, right
Walk straight ahead
Straight, straight, straight
(repeat) 
Very good! Now let’s go faster!
Turn left, left, left
Turn right, right, right
Walk straight ahead
Straight, straight, straight
(repeat)

4.– ACTIVITY 3: CAN YOU TELL ME THE WAY? (7’)
P.2.3
P.2.3
TARGET LANGUAGE
Turn right
Go past
Go straight ahead
Turn left
Behind
On your right
On your left
Opposite
Next to
Between
> How to Play
In this game, the Ss must tell their classmate the correct 
way to get to the shop to buy a certain item.
> Warm-Up
Quickly review the name of the items (P.2.3) with the Ss 
and where they can buy them. Ask, “Where can you buy a 
dress?” to which they should answer, “You can buy a dress at 
the clothes shop.”. If needed, review the shops on the A3 that 
your Ss find tricky (such as charity shop, town hall, dentist, 
basketball court, football pitch, etc.).
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Pair the Ss up (S1 and S2). Put the Item memory cards (P.2.3) 
face down on the table. To do the activity, proceed as detailed 
below. We highly encourage you to model the steps with a S 
first. Say, “Let’s go explore the city!”. Then proceed as follows: 
•	 S1: Takes a bike cutout and turns over an item card.
•	 T: “What do you need to buy?”
•	 S1: “I need to buy dog food.” (or whatever item is on 
the card). 
•	 T: “Where can you buy dog food?”
•	 S2: “You can buy dog food at the pet shop.”

•	 T: “S1, you are at the bookshop.”
•	 S1: “Can you tell me the way (to the pet shop), please?”
•	 S2: Gives directions accordingly. For example: “To get 
to the pet shop, turn right. Go straight ahead and go 
past the supermarket and the sports centre. At the 
sports centre turn left. You will find the pet shop on 
your right/the pet shop is opposite the charity shop.”
> Follow-Up
Ask Ss about the location of different shops. For example: 
“John, where is the greengrocer’s?” to which they should reply, 
“The greengrocer’s is between the bakery and the charity 
shop.”
5.– ACTIVITY 5: SHOPPING LIST (VERSION 2) (8’)
P.2.5
P.2.5
> How to Play
In this game, Ss need to find three shops where they can 
buy the items on their shopping list.
> Warm-Up
Go over the items that can be bought at the shops using the 
Shopping Lists cards (P.2.5). Ask them, for example, “Where 
can you buy boots?” to which Ss must answer, “You can buy 
boots at the shoe shop.”
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Introduce the activity by saying, “It’s time to go shopping! 
Let’s see if you can buy all the items on your shopping list!”. 
Give one Shopping List card (P.2.5) to each S. The Ss should keep 
their shopping lists face up on the table in front of them. Pick one 
card of each shop (13 in total: supermarket, butcher’s, bakery, 
café, shoe shop, clothes shop, greengrocer’s, fishmonger’s, 
toyshop, newsagent’s, bookshop, ice cream parlour, pet shop) 
and mix the deck.

Hold it in the palm of your hand and start putting the cards 
face down on a pile in the middle of the table. Ss must take it 
in turns to say, “Stop!”, and flip over the last card you placed 
on the deck. Then, they need to identify the shop by saying, for 
example, “It’s the ice cream parlour.”. Whoever has ice cream 
on their card needs to say, “You can buy ice cream at the ice 
cream parlour!”. You should then mark the shopping list of 
all the Ss who have that item. You can either use counters or 
your board marker.
Every time a Ss flips a card, take it out of the deck and leave 
it aside.
The game finishes when you have run out of time, or when 
a S has completed their shopping list.
> Follow-Up
Ask the two Ss who finished first to describe their shopping 
list as follows:
•	 You can buy tomatoes at the greengrocer’s.
•	 You can buy boots at the shoe shop.
•	 You can buy fish at the fishmonger’s.
6.– PAM&PAUL BOARD GAME (15’)
P.E.M.4.1
START
FINISH
P.E.M.4
Play as many rounds of the Pam&Paul Board Game as time 
allows.
SET-UP
1.	 The game can be played individually or in groups (this is 
recommended for big groups). Each player/pair chooses 
a counter and places it on the start square.
2.	 Start the game using one of the strategies in the “Starting 
a game” section in the introduction of the TG. 
3.	 Have them roll the dice and move their counter. Depending 
on the colour of the square (category) the Ss land on, ask 
them to perform the challenge mentioned in the Board 
Game Reference Sheet.

Special squares:
•	 Square with a plane on it: follow the dotted line and 
go back to the start.
•	 Square with Billy on it: follow Billy’s footprints and do 
the challenge.
•	 Square with a bicycle on it: ride down the road and 
do the challenge.
4.	 If they perform the challenge correctly, they can stay 
on the square. If not, give them a second chance by 
rewording or giving them clues. If they still can’t get it, 
they go back to the square they were in before.
5.	 The game ends when someone reaches the finish line.
7.– TIME TO GO HOME (TR#20) (2’)
Sing the Time to Go Home song and have the Ss form a line 
before leaving the class.

> How to Play
Each S will take a food cutout from a cloth bag and their 
classmates will help them to stick it on the Supermarket sheet 
(P.2.2) by giving them instructions on where to place it.

> Warm-Up
Quickly review the prepositions using your hands: next to, 
between, behind, in front of and opposite. Then review the names 
of the different cutouts found in the cloth bag by asking, “What 
are these?/What is this?” and get the S to reply using a full 
structure, “They are cherries./It is a turkey!”. Continue in this 
manner until you have gone over all the food items.
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Put all the activity cutouts in a cloth bag. Pair up the Ss (S1 and 
S2). Tell the Ss, “Let’s put the food items in the supermarket!”. 
To do the activity, proceed as follows:
•	 S1: Takes a food cutout. 
•	 S2: “What have you got?”
•	 S1: “I’ve got lettuce.”
•	 S2: “Where does the lettuce go?”
•	 S1: “The lettuce goes ....” and places the cutout on the 
correct spot using Blu-Tack.
> Follow-Up
To follow up, ask Ss where the different items are. For example, 
“Jane, where does the lettuce go?”, to which Jane will have to 
answer, “The lettuce goes next to the cherries.”
ACTIVITY 6: FREEZE!
P.2.5
> Main Activity
The Ss sit on the floor in a circle. Tell them, “Let’s see if 
you remember what you can buy at each shop!”. Place the 
pile of Shop cards (P.2.5) face down in the middle of the circle 
and get the Ss to begin passing the ball. Tell them that when 
you say “Freeze!”, they must stop. Whenever you feel like it, 
shout out “FREEZE!” and the S holding the ball must pick up 
a card from the middle of the circle and answer the question, 
“What can you buy at the…?” as quickly as possible. Once Ss 
are used to the game you can make it more dynamic by not 
asking them the question and letting them come up with the

sentence themselves. For example:
•	 You can buy jumpers at the clothes shop.
•	 You can buy video games at the toy shop.
•	 You can buy muffins at the bakery.
NOTE: you can also play songs from the story to make it 
more dynamic. You can still say “Freeze!” every time you pause 
the song.
